meanings: verb: to bend into a different shape
examples: The wood of the guitar warped after several hours of sitting in its owner's car, which grew extremely hot in the sun.

meanings: adjective: existing across a large area or number of people
examples: As vaccine usage becomes more widespread, fewer people suffer from preventable diseases.

meanings: verb: to continue to exist; to live through bad experiences
examples: Without food or water for days, the three shipwrecked survivors had to endure great hunger and thirst as they waited for rescue.

meanings: adjective: separate and very different
examples: Studies as disparate as religion and biology have been brought together by research into what happens in the brain during a religious experience.

meanings: adjective: simple and made without skill; not processed
examples: Once he realized he had forgotten his tent, Arpit attempted to build a crude shelter out of mud, branches, and leaves.

meanings: adjective: strong and full
examples: Chris preferred watery, mild beers, but Bhavin preferred a beer with more robust flavor.

meanings: adjective: too large and difficult to handle
examples: In many military exercises, soldiers have to carry bulky backpacks for long distances to test their strength.

meanings: noun: lack of interest
examples: In an effort to fight indifference, the president of the college introduced a new, stricter grading system.

meanings: verb: to match the rule or standard
examples: Before every yearly government inspection, the cooks would chase away mice to make the restaurant look like it conformed to cleanliness guidelines.

meanings: noun: A place to find valuable information including IELTS study tips. Learn more at magoosh.com/ielts.
adjective: hard to break or damage (in a good way)
examples: Andrew only buys durable shoes—if they can't survive at least ten years of regular wear, he won't even consider buying them.

meanings: adjective: more than is needed; overly expensive
examples: Susie's wedding was extravagant, with a dinner of steak and lobster, invitations decorated with gold, and a ceremony at a castle.

meanings: noun: the time of day immediately after the sun goes down
examples: Even though the sun had set and dusk had fallen, Sara and Klaus stayed on the beach, talking and laughing into the night.

meanings: adjective: sudden and unexpected or short
examples: The careless car in front of Elle came to such an abrupt stop that she didn't have enough time to react and crashed into the car.

meanings: adjective: combining well to improve both parts
examples: Although no one of the three ingredients in a margarita is delicious alone, the tequila, lime juice, and liqueur together are complementary.

meanings: adjective: clearly unusual (used for people or behavior)
examples: Mozart was well-known for his eccentric behavior, often speaking words backward to confuse those around him.

meanings: adjective: very new and creating a big change
examples: The revolutionary discovery of antibiotics like penicillin completely changed modern medicine.

meanings: verb: to move around a large area with little direction or plan
examples: Horses roam freely across the hills of the national park.

meanings: adjective: not having any of
examples: Milly is the most serious person I know—her stories are always completely devoid of humor.

meanings: verb: to fix, especially something torn or broken
examples: Jimmy and his father had stopped talking over the years and looked forward to mending their broken relationship over the holidays.

meanings: adjective: causing a lot of disagreement
examples: When the class debate begins to bore her, Wendy loves to say something controversial and start heated arguments among her classmates.

meanings: verb: to make hard or impossible to make progress
examples: Virginia's back pains impeded her ability to work, until eventually she had to leave her job entirely.

meanings: verb: to cover part of (used for two similar things); be in the same place or time
examples: I'd like to go both to Jon's birthday party and to my little sister's concert, but they overlap by almost three hours.

meanings: verb: to cause to happen
examples: The sound of a gunshot triggered a panic in the streets, as people ran in every direction, unsure of the source.

meanings: verb: to happen at the same time
examples: Apple's announcement of the next iPhone coincided with the release of Samsung's newest phone.

meanings: verb: to completely destroy
examples: The earthquake completely demolished the old home—no walls were left standing.

meanings: verb: to be quietly angry about something somebody else did or said
examples: I resented my older brother for all the times he started fights with my friends and me as children.

meanings: adjective: not doing what is ordered
examples: The teenagers were defiant and refused to help when Mr. Niles ordered them to clean the mess they'd made during their food fight.

meanings: verb: to hold tightly onto
examples: Standing in front of the airport, Judy clung to her father's arm and begged him not to leave.

meanings: noun: an enemy
examples: The robot army became a clear foe to all humans when they stopped doing what they were told and began destroying homes.

meanings: noun: a set of rules about what to do in formal situations
examples: Jonah followed every step of the protocol carefully to make sure the experiment was performed correctly.

meanings: verb: to create a basic picture or plan quickly
examples: I sketched some of my initial thoughts before beginning work of visuals for the presentation.

meanings: adjective: helping to make happen
examples: Studying in a quiet room is conducive to learning; studying in a noisy environment makes learning harder.

meanings: adjective: not existing anymore
examples: The dodo bird has been extinct for more than 350 years—the last confirmed sighting was in 1662.

meanings: adjective: very important, necessary
examples: Sugar is an integral ingredient in any cake recipe.

meanings: adjective: happening very soon
examples: The impending doom of our world has been discussed and debated for over 2000 years.

meanings: adjective: very beautiful
examples: The crowd took thousands of pictures of the movie star in her stunning dress, which was so beautiful they couldn't look away.

meanings: adjective: without preference or bias
examples: Sports referees have to be impartial, because if we know that they prefer one team, the final result becomes arguable.

meanings: verb: to shine or reflect small bits of light
examples: The silver of her dress shimmered like diamonds every time the light hit it.

meanings: verb: to continue to do something even though it's difficult
examples: Sarah persevered through the storm, fighting through the cold and rain, to make her way home for Christmas.

meanings: verb: to take out by force
examples: Some cheeses aren't vegetarian because they're made using a liquid called "rennet," which is extracted from cow's stomachs.

meanings: adjective: very large or wide
examples: Sinbad had always known that the desert was big, but he had no idea how vast it truly was until he crossed it on foot.

meanings: adjective: continuing even though somebody tries to stop it (usually used for bad things)
examples: Sue's persistent coughing and sneezing continued until the cold developed into pneumonia and she had to get medication.

meanings: verb: to cause to separate and go in different directions
examples: Students came from many countries for English classes at our school, but after the program ended, they dispersed and never saw each other again.

meanings: adjective: polite and respectful
examples: Since Tom is usually extremely courteous, his sister was shocked when he served their guests spaghetti using only his hands.

meanings: noun: a feeling of wanting to choose one option (often a repeated preference)
examples: Although the inclination is to ride a bike nearer to parked cars, they can be more dangerous than moving ones, as a door may open in front of you.

meanings: verb: to make unclear
adjective: known by only a few
examples: While they drove past the Grand Canyon, Mr. Smith's big head obscured much of Mrs. Robinson's view, so she only saw small patches of red rock.
Many words beginning with the letter 'x' are so obscure that only a few people have ever heard of them.

meanings: adjective: very many; more than enough
examples: Although he had an abundant supply of snacks, Jim didn't want to share and lied to his guests that he only had one bag of popcorn.

meanings: verb: to change the shape from what it should be into something different
examples: The twisted mirror distorted the man's reflection, making him appear twice as tall and far too thin.

meanings: conjunction: only if
examples: Provided you study hard for the exam, you should do well enough to pass the class.

meanings: adjective: done before someone else can do it
examples: Just as Martha was about to take the only cookie left on the table, Noah preemptively grabbed it.
